newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner head sees better 1997 than 1996.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner head sees better 1997 than 1996.

text.p: Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group Kvaerner ASA said on Friday it was disappointed with its result in the first quarter, but it expected to improve full-year operating profits compared with 1996.
London-headquartered Kvaerner booked a first-quarter operating profit of 442 million crowns against 593 million crowns a year ago and a pre-tax profit of 224 million crowns versus 537 million crowns.
The comparative figures are adjusted to take into consideration Kvaerner's takeover of British conglomerate Trafalgar House Plc in April, 1996.

"Our first quarter results are below expectation, although we still anticipate a much better operating profit in 1997. compared with 1996," Erik Tonseth, Kvaerner's President and CEO, said in a statement.

"At the same time, I expect that further reductions in interest-bearing debt through the sale of assets outside the core areas, over and above the NKr 10 billion realised so far, will continue to enhance pre-tax profits," Tonseth said.
Investors reacted positively to the results and Kvaerner's share price on the Oslo bourse surged to a high at 392 crowns in the A stock and 362 crowns in the Bs.
At 0908 GMT both the A and B shares were 28 crowns up at 386 crowns and 357 crowns respectively.
